title: Sum Reduction with OpenMP Offload on NVIDIA Grace-Hopper System
problem: Optimizing sum reduction performance when offloading to GPU using OpenMP directives while considering the impacts of team count, elements per iteration, and heterogeneous CPU-GPU execution in unified memory mode.
motivation: Sum reduction is a fundamental parallel computing primitive, and efficient implementations on accelerators are critical for overall application performance.
method: The authors annotate serial sum reduction code with OpenMP target and teams directives to offload computation to NVIDIA Grace-Hopper GPU. They systematically explore different configurations by varying the number of teams, elements processed per loop iteration, and enabling simultaneous execution on both CPU and GPU in unified memory mode, measuring performance across these parameter dimensions.
key_novelty: Systematic evaluation of OpenMP reduction optimizations on Grace-Hopper architecture with specific focus on heterogeneous CPU-GPU co-execution patterns in unified memory mode.
contributions: Evaluation of OpenMP directives for GPU-offloaded sum reduction on NVIDIA Grace-Hopper system
Analysis of optimization parameters (team count, elements per iteration, unified memory allocation location) and their impact on reduction performance
Demonstration of 6.120X-20.906X speedup achieving 89-95% of peak GPU memory bandwidth efficiency
Investigation of heterogeneous CPU-GPU co-execution enabling 1.067-2.484X speedup over GPU-only execution

metrics.speedup: 6.120X to 20.906X (GPU vs baseline); 2.484X to 1.067X (CPU-GPU co-execution vs GPU-only)
metrics.other: 89-95% of peak GPU memory bandwidth efficiency
